reason: The single cited passage (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces, hindrance of grain boundary sliding and dislocation movement, increased high-temperature strength and ductility peaking at 0.5 at% Hf, and nearly unchanged room-temperature performance. The density premise is not explicitly mentioned in the cited text but is a minor, plausible inference from the small Hf addition.
premises: Hf addition (~0.5 at%) to a dual-phase refractory HEA forms fine Hf-rich precipitates at phase interfaces
These precipitates hinder dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at high temperature
This markedly enhances high-temperature strength and ductility
Overall alloy density stays nearly unchanged compared to Hf-free baseline
